figures.caption: Saturation returns sixteen processed samples and six clipped sums before caller publication.
figures.alt: Six annotated panels at mix_ready show returns sixteen and six, unchanged input halfwords, saturated output and caller words sixteen,99,99,99. Exact sums positive 40000 and negative 40000 become 32767 and minus 32768. Exact endpoint sums remain unchanged and do not count as clipping. Wrapping output is still zero.

figures.caption: The wrapping return leaves the earlier saturation counts saved in memory.
figures.alt: Five annotated panels at wrap_ready show current returns sixteen and zero, complete saturated and wrapping samples and caller words sixteen,sixteen,six,99. Positive 40000 wraps to minus 25536 and negative 40000 wraps to 25536. The saved clipping count six belongs to the earlier saturating call; the wrapping count store is still ahead.

figures.caption: The completed comparison preserves six clipped samples beside sixteen wrapping samples.
figures.alt: Five annotated panels at comparison_ready show current returns sixteen and zero, both complete 32-byte output slices, and caller words sixteen,sixteen,six,sixteen. Saturated and wrapping values agree for representable sums and differ for the six overflow cases. Input and guards remain unchanged; the later exit service has not executed.

figures.caption: One vector group and one scalar sample produce four clipped results.
figures.alt: Six annotated panels show a fresh nine-sample run at mix_ready. Return registers are nine processed and four clipped. The first vector group contributes three clipped lanes; the scalar ninth sample contributes one. Both ninth inputs are minus 20000 and the output at 0x100101a4 is bytes 00 80. Caller result words remain 99, the wrapping buffer is untouched and logical suffixes are preserved.
